classification.difficultyReason: The substitution is supplied; rearrange the cubic into the tangent triple-angle form and choose three angle branches giving distinct roots.

content.prompt:
Solve the equation $3x^3-3x^2-9x+1=0$. Give your answers correct to two decimal places.

Hint: Let $x=\tan\theta$.

answer.worked:
Let $x=\tan\theta$.
$$\begin{align*}3x^3-3x^2-9x+1&=0\\3x^3-9x&=3x^2-1\\x^3-3x&=\frac{3x^2-1}{3}\\\frac{3x-x^3}{1-3x^2}&=\frac13\\\tan3\theta&=\frac13.\end{align*}$$
The values $x=\pm\frac{1}{\sqrt3}$, which make the denominator zero, do not satisfy the original cubic. Let $\alpha=\tan^{-1}(\frac{1}{3})$. Three distinct roots arise from
$$\theta=\frac{\alpha}{3},\quad\frac{\alpha+\pi}{3},\quad\frac{\alpha+2\pi}{3}.$$
Substituting into $x=\tan\theta$ gives
$$x\approx0.11,\ 2.26,\ -1.37\qquad\text{(2 decimal places)}.$$
